citations.title: Health informatics workforce: An update from the HIMSS workforce survey
citations.what_it_says: Reports Epic-certified application analyst median compensation of $95K-$120K with senior/consulting roles exceeding $150K, and lists Epic certification as the most-cited hiring requirement among health-system IT employers.

citations.authors: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC)
citations.title: Hospital EHR Vendors — Health IT Dashboard: Market Share of Certified Health IT Vendors Reported by Hospitals Participating in the CMS EHR Incentive Programs
citations.journal: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, ONC
citations.what_it_says: ONC's Health IT Dashboard, drawing on CMS EHR Incentive Program reporting, shows Epic Systems as the leading certified EHR vendor among U.S. non-federal acute care hospitals, with a disproportionately high share among large hospitals and health systems.

citations.title: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics: Physical Therapists; Occupational Therapists; Computer and Information Systems Managers
citations.what_it_says: Provides 2024 median wages establishing the clinical baseline (PT $99K, OT $96K) against which Epic analyst/consultant compensation premiums are measured.

citations.authors: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
citations.title: 2024 ONC Health IT Workforce Brief
citations.what_it_says: Confirms sustained growth in clinical informatics and EHR-analyst roles, noting vendor-gated certifications (Epic, Oracle Health) as primary access constraints for new entrants.
